featuredProject.eyebrow: Featured · Node.js · OpenAI API · GitHub Apps
featuredProject.title: AI-Powered Code Review Assistant
featuredProject.description: A GitHub App that analyzes pull requests and posts structured, line-anchored review comments using OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini.
highlights: Detects context-sensitive issues, such as race conditions and cross-file anti-patterns, that standard linting misses.
Engineered diff chunking and ±25-line context fetching to keep large PRs within LLM token limits.
Built a MongoDB-backed React/Vite dashboard that visualizes issues by severity and category.
Secured the pipeline with HMAC-verified webhooks, with structured logging via Winston and CI through GitHub Actions.

projects.title: PulseGrid — Load Balancer Visualizer
projects.description: A real-time load balancer simulator that compares five scheduling algorithms across a virtual server pool, with live telemetry streamed to a React dashboard.
highlights: Built a custom Indexed Min-Heap with O(1) peek and O(log N) updates, powering two of the five scheduling strategies.
Engineered a Predictive Headroom scheduler using Linear Regression, cutting CPU load standard deviation from 15.72 to 3.15 — roughly an 80% improvement over Weighted Round Robin.
Built a WebSocket telemetry layer sustaining 10Hz broadcasts, with backpressure-aware frame dropping at a 64KB buffer threshold so slow clients never stall the server.
Visualized live load distribution across the server pool with React and Recharts, so each algorithm's behavior can be compared side by side.

photo.alt: Dev Agarwal, Flutter and cross-platform mobile engineer based in Pune

storyParagraphs: I build software that ships — and I care about why it works.

At Centralogic, I delivered a Leave Management module that cut HR processing effort by 40% and a candidate assessment platform serving 500+ concurrent users. That's where I learned what production constraints actually feel like.

Since then I've been deepening my fundamentals: DSA and system design in C++, and projects like PulseGrid, where I built a custom Indexed Min-Heap and a regression-based scheduler that cut load variance by about 80% against Weighted Round Robin.

Outside engineering, I coached badminton at the competitive level for six years, running tournaments for 100+ participants. It taught me communication, execution under pressure, and working with very different personalities.
I'm now targeting SDE roles at product-based companies, where I can apply both production experience and strong CS fundamentals.
